Order 
This SEVENTH application under Section 439 of CPC has been filed by applicant Pawan Kumar for grant of bail, who has been arrested on 28-10- 2021 in connection with Crime No.777 of 2020 registered at Police Station Dehat, District Bhind (MP) for offences punishable under Sections 420,
506, 466, 467, 468, 471, 171, 193 & 201 of IPC.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn by Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 23rd of February, 2022 passed in MCRC No.7894 of 2022.
Second application was rejected on merits vide order dated 13th of May, 2022 passed by Coordinate Bench of this Court in MCRC No.17875 of 2022.

Third application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 9th of December,
2022 passed by Coordinate Bench of this Court in MCRC No.40360 of 2022.
Fourth application was rejected vide order dated 27th of March, 2023 passed by Coordinate Bench of this Court in MCRC No.7020 of 2023.
Fifth application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 11th of September,

sentences.text: Sixth application was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 28th of November, 2023 passed in MCRC No. 47594 of 2023, with liberty to applicant to renew the prayer after material witnesses are examined.

As per the case of prosecution, Rahul S/o Shri Ramnaresh submitted a written complaint to PS Dehat, District Bhind on 16-12-2019 inter alia alleging that Pawan Kumar (applicant) introducing himself as a Naval Officer, cheated him of Rs.6,40,000/- on the pretext of getting him job in Indian Navy.
On basis of this complaint, PS Dehat Distt. Bhind registered FIR No.777 of 2020 for offences punishable under Sections 420 and 506 of IPC and proceeded with the investigation.
The statements of complainant and witnesses were recorded.
The forged and fabricated documents sent by applicant accused Pawan Kumar to the complainant from time to time pertaining to his status as a Naval Officer, were seized.
On 28.10.2021, applicant -accused Pawan Kumar was arrested.

During interrogation, applicant- accused Pawan Kumar disclosed the names of co-accused Manish,
Principal Singh and Gurtaj Singh in whose accounts, the money was deposited by the complainant.

The bank accounts of applicant and co-accused were verified, where it was disclosed that the money sent by complainant was transferred in the accounts of applicant and co-accused and it was withdrawn by them from time to time.

On the basis of of facts came in light in the investigation,
prosecution for offences under Sections 466, 467, 468, 471, 171, 193 and 201 of IPC was added.
After completion of investigation, Final Report was filed on 26-01-2022 and trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, relying upon order dated 06-02-2018 passed by Apex Court in case of Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [Criminal Appeal No. 227 of 2018 arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 151 of 2018],
contends that grant of bail is a general rule and putting a person in jail is an exception.

sentences.text: Applicant is in custody for approximately 28 months.
There is no likelihood of influencing or tampering with evidence.
Trial is underway.
Therefore, applicant deserves to be released on bail.

Learned Counsel referring to cross-examination of complainant-Rahul (PW1), Anita (PW2) and Ramnaresh Jatav (PW3), contends that complainant and his parents have admitted in cross-examination that complainant Rahul was not in direct contact with the applicant.
Learned Counsel referring to various inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of these witnesses, submits that prosecution is doubtful.
Learned Counsel further contends that Rahul (PW1) has admitted all suggestions given by the defence which exonerates applicant from the alleged offence.
Learned Counsel specifically referring to Para 25 of cross-examination of Rahul (PW1), submits that Rahul has admitted that no joining letter was sent by Pawan Kumar to him.
Pawan Kumar has not promised to get him job.
Police has got his signature on complaint (Ex.P2) which was not typed in his presence.
Learned Counsel further referring to statement of Vikas Bansal (PW6), submits that witness of seizure memo (Ex.P11) did not support the prosecution.
Learned Counsel further submits that all the material witnesses have been examined.
Therefore, there is no likelihood of tampering with evidence.
Applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the application and submits that complainant Rahul (PW1) has admitted suggestion of defence in his cross-examination only, whereas in examination-in-chief Rahul (PW1) has supported the prosecution and made specific allegation with regard to cheating and forgery by applicant.

Learned Counsel for the State further contends that the Pawan Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85833288/
2 evidence with regard to fabrication and forgery of documents relating to Indian Navy is still to be produced before the trial Court, therefore, all the material witnesses have not been examined.

sentences.text: Considering the rejection of earlier bail applications on merits, the applicant may not be released on bail.
Heard Counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Examination-in-chief of Rahul (PW1)
was recorded on 15-09-2022.
Thereafter, the matter was adjourned for production of certain original documents.
Further, examination-in-chief was recorded on 18-12-2022.
Thereafter, he was further examined in chief on 11-12-2023.
He was cross- examined on 12-11-2023.
Meanwhile, many things transpired between the parties and thereafter, in his cross-examination, Rahul (PW1) started admitting all suggestions given by the defence.

It would not be appropriate to comment on merit of the evidence of complainant Rahul (PW1) but in view of laid down by Supreme Court in case of Khujji alias Surendra Tiwari vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in (1991) 3 SCC 627, the Court need to conscious of factual matrix which transpires between recording of examination- in-chief and cross-examination.

entities.text: Khujji alias Surendra Tiwari vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in (1991) 3 SCC 627
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: One petition under Section 482 of CrPC was filed by applicant Pawan Kumar for quashment of FIR on the basis of compromise between the parties.

This MCRC No. 23750 of 2023 was considered and rejected by this Court vide order dated 20th of September,
2023.
It indicates the reason for admission of all suggestions of the defence by the complainant.
There is no material change in the circumstances after rejection of earlier bail applications of applicant on merits vide orders dated 13th of May, 2022 and 27th of March, 2023.
The evidence of prosecution with regard to alleged forgery is still to produce before the trial Court.
The witnesses relating to this aspect, are also material witnesses, which are yet to be examined.

Considering all aforementioned aspects of the matter and the fact that impersonation as Navy Officer for cheating has larger ramification, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant does not deserve to be released on bail.
Accordingly, this seventh repeat bail application filed under Section 439 of CrPC is hereby dismissed.

(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE MKB Pawan Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85833288/
